title: Why .NET was born
sub: Windows programs before 2002 and what went wrong
cards/0/body:
Serious apps were written in C++ against the raw Win32 API. Quick forms were built in Visual Basic 6. Components written in different languages talked to each other through COM.

It worked, but it hurt: manual memory management, leaks and crashes. Installing one app could break another.
cards/1/body:
Apps shared DLLs in a system folder. A new app would install its own version of a library over the old one, and an older app would stop starting.

People called this DLL hell.
cards/2/options/0: One app replaces a shared library with its own version and breaks other apps
cards/2/options/1: Too many DLLs in an app folder
cards/2/explain: .NET fixed this with versioned, strong-named assemblies, and later by letting each app carry its own dependencies.
cards/3/body:
Since 1995 Java had promised "write once, run anywhere". Code compiles to bytecode, a virtual machine runs it, and a garbage collector cleans up memory.

Microsoft built its own Java (J++), added Windows-only extensions and lost a lawsuit to Sun. It needed a platform of its own.
cards/4/body:
The ideas are close to Java, but built for Windows and for many languages:

CLR: the runtime. JIT, garbage collection, type safety.
BCL: a large standard library.
C#: a new language. Its lead designer is Anders Hejlsberg, who had already created Turbo Pascal and Delphi.
cards/4/deep: C# and the CLI (Common Language Infrastructure) were standardized at ECMA (ECMA-334 and ECMA-335) back in 2001-2002. That let others build their own implementation, and that is how Mono appeared.
cards/5/task: Find the year .NET Framework 1.0 came out and see which systems it ran on.
cards/6/q: Match each part of .NET to its role
cards/6/pairs/2/1: A new language for the platform
cards/6/pairs/3/1: The old way to connect components
cards/7/q: Which problems did .NET solve? Select all that apply.
cards/7/options/2: Different languages could not easily work together
cards/7/options/3: Apps did not run on Linux
cards/7/explain: For its first 14 years, official .NET ran only on Windows. Linux came later, first through Mono.
cards/8/q: Who is the lead designer of C#?
cards/8/explain: Gosling created Java, and Stroustrup created C++.
